title: ConnectorEvent
description: Versioned envelope for every event a connector reports to the backend (inbound messages, send acknowledgements, failures, delivery receipts, connection changes). Simulated traffic from WING-006's MockConnector uses the explicit `mock.*` types, which are only valid with `platform: mock`, and live `message.*` types are never valid with `platform: mock`, so simulated success can never be mistaken for a real one. Deduplication: a message is identified by (platform, external_message_id) within the user scope (`user_id`); replaying an event with an already-seen key must not create a second message or a second state transition. Exact replays of the same envelope are also recognisable by `event_id`. The `text` field carries private content: it may be persisted but must never be written to application logs. See docs/architecture.md. Since contract 1.3.0 an inbound payload may describe a notification- or unofficial-API-sourced event (`kind`, `identity`, `truncated`, `content_hidden`, `source`, `sender_label`, `external_conversation_id`); only a linked, complete `chat_message` becomes a message that the automation pipeline sees, everything else is stored as a notice and never replied to (ADR 0008). A device that has no platform message ID must send a stable synthetic one (for example a hash of the notification key and post time) so that duplicates are recognized.

event_id.description: Unique per emitted event (UUID). A connector re-sending the same event must reuse the same event_id.

connection_id.description: Wingman connection that produced the event.

user_id.description: User scope. Every event belongs to exactly one Wingman user; consumers must reject events whose connection does not belong to this user.

external_message_id.description: Platform-assigned message ID. Required (non-null) for received, acknowledged and delivery events; null for send failures with no platform ID and for connection events.

external_thread_id.description: Platform conversation/thread ID, when the platform has one.

occurred_at.description: When the event happened at the source (UTC, Z).

observed_at.description: When the connector observed/emitted it (UTC, Z). Optional.

event_type.description: Live types: `message.received` (inbound message observed), `message.send_acknowledged` (transport accepted our outbound message: drives `sent`), `message.send_failed` (attempt failed: drives `failed`), `message.delivery_receipt` (platform reported delivery: drives `delivered`), `connection.status_changed`, `connection.capabilities_changed`. Mock-transport types (platform `mock` only, payload carries a `mock` block): `mock.inbound_message_injected` (test harness injected an inbound message; ingested like message.received), `mock.outbound_send_acknowledged`, `mock.outbound_send_failed`, `mock.delivery_receipt_simulated` (simulated counterparts of the live send outcomes).

mock_block.description: Simulation metadata. Only on mock.* events.

sequence.description: Monotonic step number inside the scenario, for deterministic ordering.

inbound_message_payload.description: Inbound message or notice. The 1.3.0 fields are optional; absent means `kind: chat_message`, `identity: linked`, `truncated: false`, `content_hidden: false` (the 1.2.0 meaning).

kind.description: (1.3.0) What the event is. Only `chat_message` can enter the automation pipeline; `match`, `like_comment`, `expiry`, `system` and `unknown` are stored as notices and never replied to.

external_conversation_id.description: (1.3.0) Platform conversation or match ID when the source exposes one (notifications often do not).

sender_label.description: (1.3.0) The sender as the source displayed it (e.g. a first name in a notification title). A label, not an identity: never used to merge people. Private: never log.

identity.description: (1.3.0) `linked`: a stable platform identifier ties the event to exactly one contact and thread. `unlinked`: only a label is known. `ambiguous`: the label matches more than one person or thread. Only `linked` events can become messages.

truncated.description: (1.3.0) The source cut the text (e.g. a notification preview). Never enters the pipeline.

content_hidden.description: (1.3.0) The source hid the content (lock-screen privacy, sensitive-content filter); `text` is then empty. Never enters the pipeline.

source.description: (1.3.0) How the device observed it; must equal the connection's `transport` when given.

outbound_message_id.description: Wingman message ID the dispatcher asked the connector to send.

idempotency_key.description: Dispatcher send key. The connector performs at most one transport send per key.
